ERBB2

UniProt ID: P04626
Organism: Homo sapiens
Review Status: DRAFT
📝 Provide Detailed Feedback
421 Annotations 1 Core Function 199 References 1 Documents Raw YAML

Gene Description

ERBB2/HER2 is an ERBB-family plasma-membrane receptor tyrosine kinase that acts as a preferred signaling partner for other ligand-bound ERBB receptors. It lacks a known soluble ligand of its own but forms active homodimers and heterodimers with EGFR, ERBB3, and ERBB4, trans-autophosphorylates receptor tyrosines, and recruits adaptor and effector proteins that activate MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling. ERBB2 also has nuclear signaling roles and is frequently amplified or mutated in cancers.

Core Functions

ERBB-family receptor tyrosine kinase coreceptor activity in plasma-membrane signaling receptor dimers, phosphorylating tyrosine residues that couple ERBB2-containing receptors to MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling.

Molecular Function:
transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
Directly Involved In:
epidermal growth factor receptor signaling pathway ERBB2-EGFR signaling pathway ERBB2-ERBB3 signaling pathway phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B signal transduction
Cellular Locations:
plasma membrane

id: P04626
gene_symbol: ERBB2
product_type: PROTEIN
status: DRAFT
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: >-
  ERBB2/HER2 is an ERBB-family plasma-membrane receptor tyrosine kinase that
  acts as a preferred signaling partner for other ligand-bound ERBB receptors.
  It lacks a known soluble ligand of its own but forms active homodimers and
  heterodimers with EGFR, ERBB3, and ERBB4, trans-autophosphorylates receptor
  tyrosines, and recruits adaptor and effector proteins that activate MAPK and
  PI3K-AKT signaling. ERBB2 also has nuclear signaling roles and is frequently
  amplified or mutated in cancers.

- term:
    id: GO:0005524
    label: ATP binding
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000002
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - InterPro:IPR000719
  - InterPro:IPR016245
  - InterPro:IPR017441
  review:
    summary: ATP binding is required for catalysis by the ERBB2 kinase domain.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: ATP binding is mechanistically correct for the kinase domain but less informative than
      the core tyrosine kinase activity.
- term:
    id: GO:0005634
    label: nucleus
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:16314522
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: ERBB2 can undergo endocytosis-dependent nuclear translocation.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Nuclear localization is experimentally supported for full-length or intracellular ERBB2,
      but it is a secondary localization relative to the core plasma-membrane receptor pool.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:16314522
      supporting_text: 'Endosomal transport of ErbB-2: mechanism for nuclear entry of the cell surface
        receptor.'

- term:
    id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000052
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: ERBB2 has been detected in the nucleoplasm in high-throughput imaging.

      central localization than plasma membrane and endosomal trafficking compartments.
- term:
    id: GO:0005737
    label: cytoplasm
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000120
  qualifier: located_in
  supporting_entities:
  - ARBA:ARBA00026971
  - UniProtKB:P70424
  - ensembl:ENSMUSP00000053897
  - UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0086
  review:
    summary: Cytoplasmic ERBB2 reflects internalized receptor and cytoplasmic C-terminal isoforms.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Cytoplasmic localization is plausible for internalized and truncated ERBB2 species, but
      the canonical receptor is a plasma-membrane protein.

    label: cytosol

  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000052
  qualifier: located_in

    summary: Cytosolic signal is a broad localization for internalized or truncated ERBB2 species.

      membrane anchored.
- term:
    id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
  evidence_type: EXP
  original_reference_id: PMID:31138794
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: ERBB2 is a type I plasma-membrane receptor and the cited evidence places
      ERBB2-containing signaling complexes at the plasma membrane.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Plasma membrane localization is the canonical localization for full-length ERBB2; the
      many Reactome TAS events are redundant event-level supports for the same receptor location but
      are biologically sound.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:31138794
      supporting_text: SORLA regulates endosomal trafficking and oncogenic fitness of HER2.

- term:
    id: GO:0006468
    label: protein phosphorylation
  evidence_type: TAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:10851066
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: ERBB2 is a receptor tyrosine kinase whose direct reaction is tyrosine phosphorylation.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: GO:0006468 is a broad protein-phosphorylation process; the ERBB2 kinase specifically
      catalyzes peptidyl-tyrosine phosphorylation.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0018108
      label: peptidyl-tyrosine phosphorylation
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:10851066
      supporting_text: Interaction between protein tyrosine phosphatase and protein tyrosine kinase
        is involved in androgen-promoted growth of human prostate cancer cells.
- term:
    id: GO:0007165
    label: signal transduction
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:10572067
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: The cited ErbB-1/ErbB-2 heterodimer study supports the more specific MAP kinase
      activation already curated from the same paper.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: GO:0007165 is an uninformative ancestor for ERBB2; the same evidence supports positive
      regulation of MAP kinase activity downstream of ErbB heterodimers.

    - id: GO:0043406
      label: positive regulation of MAP kinase activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:10572067
      supporting_text: Dominance of ErbB-1 heterodimers in lung epithelial cells overexpressing
        ErbB-2. Both ErbB-1 and ErbB-2 contribute significantly to tumorigenicity.

core_functions:
- description: >-
    ERBB-family receptor tyrosine kinase coreceptor activity in plasma-membrane
    signaling receptor dimers, phosphorylating tyrosine residues that couple
    ERBB2-containing receptors to MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004714
    label: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
  directly_involved_in:

    label: epidermal growth factor receptor signaling pathway
  - id: GO:0038134
    label: ERBB2-EGFR signaling pathway
  - id: GO:0038133
    label: ERBB2-ERBB3 signaling pathway
  - id: GO:0043491
    label: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B signal transduction
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
